newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet's Doniambo nickel output up in 96.
newsitem.headline: Eramet's Doniambo nickel output up in 96.

text.p: French nickel producer Eramet said on Friday that output at its Doniambo nickel plant in New Caledonia reached 53,413 tonnes in 1996, up two percent over 1995.
"Annual production capacity at the plant is now around 55,000 tonnes in line with the ongoing development plan," Eramet said in a statement.
Eramet generated 2.677 billion francs from nickel sales in 1996, a rise of 3.5 percent over 1995.
The increase resulted mostly from a 7.5 percent rise in deliveries to 54,596 tonnes.
Despite a decline in world nickel consumption, Eramet benefited from a growth in stainless steel production in Asia, a region that accounts for 40 percent of the group's nickel deliveries.
Average nickel selling prices in French francs declined 3.5 percent, a rise in the dollar against the franc partially offsetting a decline in international nickel prices expressed in dollars.
Rapid steel sales fell 11.8 percent to 1.232 billlion francs in 1996, following a 13.1 percent fall in deliveries to 25,228 tonnes.
This followed a decline in rapid steel demand, that accelerated during the second half of the year, notably in Europe.
